parsed.paper_uuid: Gary Habermas - Chapter 007 - Which Scholars Accept the Facts for the Resurrection - Gary Habermas

source_selection.exact_source_expression: when I say I I say a critical scholar ha- it I this is defined in volume one in particular has the following uh characteristics. They have a terminal degree. ... a terminal degree and they've worked in some area where they know what's going on and I list the areas.
source_selection.reason: This is a definitional criterion that can be encoded as a predicate over scholars with explicit fields for degree, field, and publication. It is the load-bearing definition for the survey methodology and is precise enough to formalize.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A scholar qualifies as a 'critical scholar' for the minimal-facts survey iff they hold a terminal degree in a relevant field (New Testament, Old Testament, history, philosophy, archaeology, or world religions) and have demonstrated competence in the relevant research area, typically evidenced by publication or comparable research output.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def IsCriticalScholar (s : Scholar) : Prop := s.hasTerminalDegree ∧ s.field ∈ relevantFields ∧ s.hasDemonstratedCompetence

symbol_table.formal_definition: structure Scholar where name : String; hasTerminalDegree : Bool; field : Field; hasDemonstratedCompetence : Bool
symbol_table.reader_meaning: An individual whose opinion is being counted in the survey.

symbol_table.formal_definition: Finset Field := {NewTestament, OldTestament, History, Philosophy, Archaeology, WorldReligions}
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Fields Habermas explicitly accepts as relevant.

symbol_table.formal_definition: Bool, intended to be witnessed by publication or comparable research output
symbol_table.reader_meaning: Real knowledge of the research area.

explicit_premises: Terminal degree includes PhD, D.Theol., D.Phil., and analogous degrees.
Relevant fields include New Testament, Old Testament, history, philosophy, archaeology, and world religions.
Demonstrated competence may be evidenced by publication, research output, or comparable scholarly engagement.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one Scholar satisfying IsCriticalScholar; otherwise the definition is vacuous for the survey.

verification_controls.interpretation: Lean corpus was not searched and no Lean environment was invoked in this run.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A precise Lean-style definition of the critical-scholar criterion as stated in the transcript.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the definition matches Habermas's full intended criteria, whether the field list is exhaustive, and whether any actual scholar satisfies it.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the two stated components (terminal degree and field competence) but does not encode the speaker's lenient exceptions for non-PhD researchers such as G. A. Wells.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: This definition underpins the survey methodology discussed in A04, A06, and A08.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: the reason you target the ones that are publishing is because we when we have a scholarly consensus, we want it to be an informed group of scholars. ... we want people who've actually studied the resurrection research and published an opinion.
source_selection.reason: This is a methodological principle linking publication in the field to informed opinion. It can be formalized as a predicate over scholars and used to restrict the consensus sample.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: A scholar has an informed opinion on the resurrection iff they have published in the field of resurrection research or otherwise demonstrated sustained engagement with the relevant literature.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: def HasInformedOpinion (s : Scholar) : Prop := s.publishedInResurrectionField ∨ s.demonstratedSustainedEngagement

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The scholar has published peer-reviewed or comparable work on the resurrection.
The scholar has engaged the research literature in a sustained way, e.g., through interviews or research-type settings.

explicit_premises: Publication in the field is a reliable indicator of informed opinion.
Sustained engagement with the literature can substitute for publication in some cases.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one scholar with an informed opinion for the consensus argument to be non-vacuous.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal predicate for informed opinion based on publication or sustained engagement.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the predicate is too permissive or too restrictive, and whether it matches Habermas's actual inclusion criteria.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The definition captures the publication criterion but leaves 'sustained engagement' vague, which may require further specification.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Directly supports the response to objection A08.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: The six facts aren't just agreed on by Christians; even atheist and very liberal scholars grant them.
source_selection.reason: This is a consensus claim that can be formalized as a statement about the distribution of agreement across ideological groups, given a sample of scholars.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: Given a sample of scholars S, if the minimal facts are accepted by a substantial number of scholars across ideological spectra (including atheist and very liberal scholars), then the consensus is not solely a Christian bias artifact.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: theorem consensus_not_bias_artifact (S : Finset Scholar) (facts : Finset Fact) (h : ∀ f ∈ facts, ∃ s ∈ S, s.ideology = Atheist ∧ Accepts s f) : ¬ IsChristianBiasArtifact S facts

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The scholar accepts the fact as historically established.
The consensus is an artifact of sampling only Christians.

explicit_premises: There exist atheist or very liberal scholars who accept the minimal facts.
Acceptance by such scholars is evidence against a purely Christian bias explanation.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: The sample S must contain at least one atheist or very liberal scholar who accepts the facts.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal schema for arguing that consensus is not a Christian bias artifact if non-Christian scholars accept the facts.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: The actual empirical distribution of scholars and their views, and whether the sample is representative.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization captures the logical structure but abstracts away from the specific six facts and the actual survey data.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: They say, 'People wonder why we don't have any words that are purported from the resurrected Jesus in the Gospels. There's a reason for it. Dead men don't rise. And so for us, his life ends on Good Friday evening.'
source_selection.reason: This is a claim about a presupposition held by the Jesus Seminar. It can be formalized as a conditional: if one presupposes that resurrections do not occur, then one's conclusions about resurrection are pre-loaded.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: If a research program presupposes that resurrections do not occur, then its conclusions about the resurrection are determined by that presupposition rather than by the evidence.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: theorem presupposition_determines_conclusion (P : ResearchProgram) (h : Presupposes P (¬ ∃ r, Resurrection r)) : PreLoadedConclusion P

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The program assumes a proposition as a starting point.
The program's conclusions are predetermined by its presuppositions.

explicit_premises: The Jesus Seminar explicitly presupposes that resurrections do not occur.
A presupposition that rules out a phenomenon precludes genuine investigation of that phenomenon.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: There must exist at least one research program that presupposes the non-occurrence of resurrections.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal schema linking presuppositions to pre-loaded conclusions.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the Jesus Seminar actually held this presupposition and whether the inference is valid in all cases.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization is abstract and does not capture the specific historical details of the Jesus Seminar.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Supports the critique of the Jesus Seminar's methodology.

source_selection.exact_source_expression: Bultmann's name is in that list, and he doesn't accept a whole lot of the verses, but he says there was a Markan pre-Markan narrative, and he only uses a few verses. ... He says, 'These early sayings go back to the very earliest Jerusalem church.' ... 'The earliest disciples preached that he was raised from the dead.'
source_selection.reason: This is a historical claim about Bultmann's views that can be formalized as a set of propositions attributed to Bultmann, with evidence citations.

formal_object.exact_proposed_statement: Rudolf Bultmann affirmed (1) a pre-Markan passion narrative, (2) that early sayings go back to the earliest Jerusalem church, and (3) that the earliest disciples preached that Jesus was raised from the dead.
formal_object.fully_qualified_declaration: theorem bultmann_affirms_early_sources : Affirms Bultmann PreMarkanPassionNarrative ∧ Affirms Bultmann EarliestJerusalemChurchSayings ∧ Affirms Bultmann EarliestDisciplesPreachedResurrection

symbol_table.reader_meaning: The scholar publicly affirmed the proposition.
There existed a passion narrative source used by Mark.

explicit_premises: Bultmann's writings are accurately represented in the transcript.
The propositions attributed to Bultmann are correctly interpreted.
assumptions_and_dependencies.non_vacuity_requirement: Bultmann must be a scholar whose views are documented.

result_and_boundary.what_is_established: A formal statement of Bultmann's alleged affirmations.
result_and_boundary.what_remains_open: Whether the historical Bultmann actually held these views and whether the citations are accurate.
result_and_boundary.encoding_fidelity_review: The formalization is a direct encoding of the transcript's claims, not an independent historical verification.
result_and_boundary.interpretive_connections: Supports the argument that even skeptical scholars accept early sources.
